questionText: Which of the following statements about IPv4 fragmentation is/are TRUE?
options: The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed only at the source of the datagram
The fragmentation of an IP datagram is performed at any IP router which finds that the size of the datagram to be transmitted exceeds the MTU
The reassembly of fragments is performed only at the destination of the datagram
The reassembly of fragments is performed at all intermediate routers along the path from the source to the destination
explanation:
Statement (A) is FALSE: In IPv4, fragmentation can occur at the source host as well as at any intermediate router along the path if the packet size exceeds the MTU of the outgoing interface.

Statement (B) is TRUE: Any IPv4 router along the path will fragment a datagram if its size is larger than the Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of the next link (provided the 'Don't Fragment' bit is not set).

Statement (C) is TRUE: In IPv4, fragment reassembly is performed exclusively at the final destination host to avoid processing overhead and buffer management complexities on intermediate routers.

Statement (D) is FALSE: Intermediate routers only forward fragments; they do not reassemble them. Reassembly happens strictly at the destination.
